answer: Stake-slashing-on-equivocation gives each identity a sonnet's fixed form: no room for two voices. Every agent locks 1,000 tokens; one identity submitting two conflicting proofs loses 30% and freezes for the next epoch. Honest agents speak with a single whisper and keep everything. A sybil running N identities must lock N x 1,000 tokens, and one duplicate commit costs 300 tokens. Reviewers spot equivocations like a lantern, linking correlated timing to unmask the swarm. Paying humans to keep each identity consistent costs N wages above the per-identity reward, so mass farming never pays.
